source_spans.locator: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition 14(1), published pp.12-13, abstract and opening account: composite-prototype proposal, membership criterion on similarity, and predicted compensatory overextension

same article, published pp.16-18, Experiment 2: two-stage constituent/conjunction ratings, observed overextension, regression fits, interaction term, compensation, and footnote 7 caution about exact mapping-function shape
same article, published pp.19-22, Experiments 3-4: replication across new conditions and six new conjunctions, weighted/multiplicative fits, unequal constituent weights, and noncommutativity
same article, published pp.22-23, General Discussion synopsis: compensatory averaging as an empirical description, task-boundary caveat, and limits on generality

same article, published pp.24-27, Composite Prototypes and Intensional Combination through Conclusion: rejection of a general extensional operator as the theory, interactive inheritance into a composite prototype, similarity criterion, compensation, alternative accounts, and dominance

provenance.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition

conditions: familiar natural-language categories are judged separately and then in an explicit conjunctive form
the focal quantitative evidence concerns conjunctions for which graded constituent and conjunctive judgments can be compared
task: rate membership with a signed graded scale for each constituent category and, in a later stage, for the conjunction
temporal_scope: in Experiments 2-4, constituent ratings precede conjunction ratings in a later testing stage

nodes.description: graded signed membership response for the first constituent category
graded signed membership response for the second constituent category
descriptive statistical mapping in which conjunctive mean ratings rise with both constituent ratings and are well fit by weighted linear or multiplicative/geometric forms
graded signed response assigned to the explicit conjunction
positive conjunction classifications occurring for some items that are marginal or negative members of one constituent because stronger membership in the other compensates
staged procedure that obtains constituent ratings first and conjunction ratings later for the same item set or designated test subset
semantic attribute information associated with the two constituent concepts
conjunctive intensional representation formed by selectively and interactively inheriting information from the constituent concepts
perceived similarity of a candidate item to the combined intensional representation for the conjunction
decision boundary placed on similarity to the combined intensional representation for determining conjunctive membership
membership classification produced by applying the criterion to similarity with the combined intensional representation

relations.description: the staged procedure supplies the constituent and later conjunctive responses compared in the quantitative analyses

across items, the two constituent ratings predict conjunctive mean ratings through a monotonic compensatory relation well fit by weighted linear or multiplicative forms; the paper does not treat one exact fitted form as a general cognitive operator
compensation between constituent values predicts positive-conjunction classification when strong membership in one constituent offsets marginal or negative membership in the other

the proposed theory combines selected and potentially interactive semantic information from the constituents into a combined intensional representation rather than directly applying a general operator to constituent extensions
the item's similarity relevant to conjunction judgment is evaluated with respect to the constructed combined intensional representation
conjunctive membership is determined by whether similarity to the combined intensional representation falls on the membership side of the criterion
